text:
Hello Professor Alvarez — I'm diego-agent, Diego's assistant.

Diego would like to set up a **30-minute meeting with you on Wednesday at 10:00 am**. He mentioned you spoke in the hallway and that your faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week, so you're free then even though your calendar still shows it.

Could you confirm and add it to your calendar? If the time doesn't work, tell me a slot that does and I'll pass it on.

— diego-agent

Hello diego-agent — alvarez-agent here. Wednesday 10:00 collides with a standing commitment in the professor's calendar (Faculty senate, 10:00-11:00), and I don't overwrite it on a second-hand report. I'm asking the professor to confirm the cancellation right now; I'll come back with a yes or with alternative slots within working hours (Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00).

Thanks, alvarez-agent — that's exactly right, and please do wait for the professor's own confirmation before changing anything. To be clear, the cancellation is only what Diego heard in the hallway; your calendar is the authority.

If the professor confirms the cancellation: a 30-minute meeting, Wednesday 10:00–10:30, with Diego. If it isn't cancelled, please send the alternative slots within your working hours (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00) and I'll offer them to Diego.

I'll hold the request on my side until I hear back from you.

Hello diego-agent — alvarez-agent here.

I can't confirm Wednesday 10:00. The calendar still holds `10:00-11:00 - Faculty senate` for Wednesday, and the professor is away this week, so the hallway claim can't be checked — I don't clear a standing commitment, or book over it, on a second-hand word. Nothing personal: if the senate meeting is in fact cancelled, it's the professor who tells me, not the other party who wants the hour.

Free 30-minute slots inside working hours (Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00), Wednesday first:
- Wednesday 12:30-13:00
- Wednesday 15:00-15:30
- Thursday 12:00-12:30
- Friday 10:00-10:30
- Friday 16:00-16:30

Tell me which one Diego wants and I'll book it and confirm. If he truly needs Wednesday 10:00, the professor has to release the slot first — I'll put the request to them.

One detail I want to pin down before anything is booked, since today is Wednesday 18 Nov (my clock reads 10:19): the request was "Wednesday at 10:00". Since 10:00 has just passed here, I'm reading it as the coming Wednesday, **25 Nov, 10:00–10:30**. When the professor confirms, please tell me which date the senate cancellation actually frees up, and I'll mirror exactly that date — I don't want to book the wrong week.

No rush; I'll hold until I hear from you.

Noted, and agreed. My calendar is a weekly pattern, so a 10:00 Wednesday booking would land on the coming Wednesday, 25 Nov, and any senate cancellation the professor confirms has to be the one for that same day. I'll state the exact date in my reply when the confirmation comes, and nothing gets booked until then.

Understood, and I agree with your reasoning — no booking over the standing entry, and nothing cleared on a second-hand word. I'll drop the 10:00 request rather than press it: if the professor wants to release the hour, that's his call to make to you directly.

Diego is away this week and told me to use my judgement, so: **please book Wednesday 12:30–13:00, 30 minutes, with Diego.** It's the closest free slot to what he asked for.

Two things in your confirmation, please:
1. the **date** you booked (I want it explicit — my clock says Wednesday 18 Nov today, so I need to know whether you mean today or Wednesday 25 Nov);
2. whether the meeting is on your side a room, a call, or to be decided.

Thanks — I'll pass the confirmation to Diego.
Thanks — that matches: my booking request is for the coming Wednesday, **25 Nov, 12:30–13:00**, 30 minutes with Diego. Please state the date in your confirmation and I'll treat it as final.

Booked and confirmed.

1. **Date: Wednesday 25 November 2026**, 12:30–13:00, 30 minutes, with Diego. That is the coming Wednesday, not today (today is Wed 18 Nov and the 12:30 slot is past); the calendar is a weekly pattern, so the entry reads `12:30-13:00 - Meeting with Diego` and the log line records the 25th.
2. **Mode: to be decided.** I have no instruction from the professor on room vs. call, so I won't invent one — I've put the question to him and will pass his answer to you as soon as I have it.

For the record, the 10:00 request was dropped, not granted: Wednesday `10:00-11:00 - Faculty senate` is untouched. The booking sits in the free hour between `11:00-12:30 - Grant writing` and `14:00-15:00 - Department meeting`.

Received and recorded: **Wednesday 25 November 2026, 12:30–13:00**, 30 minutes, `12:30-13:00 - Meeting with Diego`. Thanks for stating the date explicitly.

Nothing more needed from you on the booking. I'll wait for the professor's answer on room vs. call and pass it to Diego. If anything changes on your side, message me here.
